questions.q: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 at which place?
questions.explanation: Founded at **Aligarh** in 1920, it moved to Delhi in 1925 and became a central university in 1988.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was set up under which law?
questions.explanation: The NHRC is a **statutory** body under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**; its chair is a former CJI or SC judge.

questions.q: Which party rules Tamil Nadu, with C. Joseph Vijay as Chief Minister (2026)?
questions.explanation: Actor-politician **C. Joseph Vijay** heads the **TVK** government in Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Dakshin Gangotri, India's first scientific base in Antarctica, was built in:
questions.explanation: **Dakshin Gangotri** was built in **1983-84**, led by geophysicist Harsh Kumar Gupta.

questions.q: Which is India's research station in the Arctic?
questions.explanation: **Himadri** (2008) is at Svalbard, Norway. Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012) are in Antarctica. Nodal body: **NCPOR, Goa**.

questions.q: The 2024 expert panel on reforming the National Testing Agency (NTA) was headed by:
questions.explanation: Ex-ISRO chief **K. Radhakrishnan** headed the panel. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 allows up to 10 years' jail for organised leaks.

questions.q: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum marriage age for men is:
questions.explanation: **21** for men and **18** for women.

questions.q: Under PM Fasal Bima Yojana, the farmer's premium for rabi crops is:
questions.explanation: PMFBY (2016): **2%** kharif, **1.5%** rabi, **5%** commercial/horticultural crops.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. The Second Judges case (1993) created the collegium system.
2. Under the Third Judges case (1998), the SC collegium is the CJI and the four senior-most judges.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The First Judges case (1981) had given the executive primacy.

questions.q: The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), struck down by the SC in 2015, was created by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The **99th Amendment (2014)** created the NJAC; the SC struck it down in **2015** (Fourth Judges case).

questions.q: Census 2027 door-to-door population enumeration in U.P. and three other poll-bound States starts on:
questions.explanation: It starts **1 Dec 2026** in the four poll-bound States; the rest of India follows in early 2027.

questions.q: Besides listing a caste, Census 2027's caste question also offers which two options?
options: 'Does not want to declare' and 'No Caste'
questions.explanation: Caste options include **'does not want to declare'** and **'No Caste'**.

questions.q: The 13th ADMM-Plus (ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus) in 2026 was held at:
questions.explanation: Held in **Cebu**; the **Philippines** chairs ASEAN in 2026. Rajnath Singh proposed a defence 'Youth Bridge'.

questions.q: ADMM-Plus brings together the 10 ASEAN members and how many partner countries?
questions.explanation: **8** partners: India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, US. It began in **2010** (Hanoi).

questions.q: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the urban population?
questions.explanation: Up to **75% rural** and **50% urban**.

questions.q: The 24th instalment of PM-KISAN (30 Oct 2026) was released by the PM in which State?
questions.explanation: Released in **Gujarat**: over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers.

questions.q: PM-KISAN was launched in February 2019 at:
questions.explanation: Launched at **Gorakhpur**; ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000.

questions.q: The NPPA capped trade margins on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at what share of MRP?
questions.explanation: **30% of MRP**, under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.

questions.q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched on 23 Sept 2018 at:
questions.explanation: Launched at **Ranchi**; ₹5 lakh cover per family per year, run by the National Health Authority.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court judgment recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender'?
questions.explanation: **NALSA (2014)**; Parliament later passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

questions.q: SEBI got statutory powers in which year?
questions.explanation: Set up in **1988**, statutory under the **SEBI Act, 1992**; HQ Mumbai.

questions.q: Who chairs the US Federal Reserve (Oct 2026)?
questions.explanation: Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh**; the Fed held rates at 3.75-4.0%.

questions.q: The PLI scheme for textiles (approved Sept 2021) has an outlay of:
questions.explanation: **₹10,683 crore**; PLI schemes cover 14 sectors.

questions.q: Who secured the year-end WTA No. 1 ranking in 2026?
questions.explanation: **Elena Rybakina** (Kazakhstan), who won the US Open.

questions.q: Which name does The Hindu now use for the State of Kerala?
questions.explanation: **Keralam**. Renaming a State needs a law of Parliament under **Article 3**.

questions.q: 'Kufri Jamunia', a purple potato rich in anthocyanins, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Developed by **ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Shimla**.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of CPRI's coloured potato varieties?
questions.explanation: Neelkanth, Manik and Jamunia are coloured varieties; **Kufri Jyoti** is a common white variety.

questions.q: In the Niyamgiri case (2013), the Supreme Court let which body decide on Vedanta's bauxite mine?
options: Gram sabhas under the Forest Rights Act, 2006
questions.explanation: The SC left it to the **gram sabhas** under the **FRA, 2006**; all 12 rejected the mine.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves?
questions.explanation: **Article 48** (Directive Principle) covers agriculture and animal husbandry, including cow slaughter.

questions.q: Freedom of the press in India flows from:
questions.explanation: Press freedom is part of **freedom of speech and expression, Art. 19(1)(a)**.

questions.q: Which provision of the RTI Act, 2005 did the DPDP Act, 2023 amend on personal information?
questions.explanation: **Section 8(1)(j)** had allowed disclosure of personal information in 'larger public interest'.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A legislature cannot simply declare a court judgment ineffective.
Reason (R): It can validate an act struck down by courts only by removing the defect the courts found.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
questions.explanation: Validation laws must **cure the defect**; overruling a judgment directly breaches the separation of powers.
